newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH GOVT DECIDES ON 1998 SPENDING.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH GOVT DECIDES ON 1998 SPENDING.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Thursday that the new Socialist government had completed its spending package for 1998.
"The spending is settled," the minister said as he left a meeting at the office of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin. Details could be known in early September," he said.
He would not comment when asked whether the spending increase would be held to the rise in inflation.
Jospin spent the day putting the finishing touches on the spending package that reports suggested could contain the smallest rise in expenditure in a decade.
Government sources had said the aim was to keep the spending rise to less than two percent and one newspaper said on Friday that Jospin could even push for a cap of 1.2 percent.

Jospin's aim has been to ensure that the spending allocation is in line with a pledge to limit France's public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1998 in preparation for European monetary union while rebalancing spending according to new priorities.
